NormalizeParameters pads shorter arrays but preserves oversized ones, so its must-have-length description is stronger than its implementation. Public wrappers remain mutable array carriers; no redesign is proposed.

ownership_qualification: ReadOnlyMemory is not an immutable-storage or clearing-owner contract. Tlv.Value and key getters borrow their owners; Memory-returning TLV helpers transfer writable output. DecodeDictionary transfers values typed ReadOnlyMemory without a disposable clear owner, and clearing a later mutable copy does not erase the original or abandoned parse copies. The raw HID paragraph likewise cannot make original readonly returned secret storage disappear by clearing a copy. Preserve this as a caller/API ownership qualification for C005/C006/C013 and the B5 boundary; recommend existing disposable/writable owners where available, without inventing a breaking API or writable-cast workaround. For C017, retain the contributor policy favoring disposable reference-type owners while correcting its rationale: a struct copy duplicates an array reference, not the array bytes, so clearing the shared backing array affects all aliases. The hazard is shared mutation and ambiguous lifetime/disposal ownership, not an inability for ZeroMemory to reach aliases. The root CLAUDE wording is a narrow shared-editor dependency, not an added C primary population.
test_hook_qualification: For C014, internal observer comments saying callbacks must never retain private values need a precise test-only exception: the zeroing tests intentionally retain array references to inspect them after the production owner clears them. They must not mutate live private data or transfer production ownership. Preserve these observation scopes rather than claiming the tests obey a blanket no-retention instruction or prove erasure of unobserved runtime/native copies.
allocation_failure_qualification: For C013, RSAParameters.DeepCopy allocates several private arrays in an object initializer before NormalizeParameters enters its try. Failure of a later allocation can abandon earlier owned private clones without explicit clearing; observer-throw fixtures occur after that allocation stage and do not cover it. This is a conditional source-derived lifetime concern, not an executed OOM repro, exploit claim or authorization for a refactor.
